seo.title: What is new
seo.description: Every change OpenMixer brought, to Zynthian and to the console, in plain words, with the pages that explain each one and, for Zynthian, the pull requests behind it.

hero.title: What is new
hero.lede: Every change OpenMixer brought, in two halves. On Zynthian, one paragraph per change: a change with a page of its own says what it is, where it appears, what you do and what you see, with pictures from a Raspberry Pi 5 running the Open-Mixer fork, and every merged pull request is listed under its change. On the console, one paragraph per group of changes since openmixer 0.2.0, with the pages that explain it.

index.consoleLede: The console's changes since openmixer 0.2.0, the last published release, one paragraph per group, each with the pages of the console's documentation that explain it.

page.prs: The pull requests this page covers
page.noPrs: None merged yet: this page says what is coming.

curves.title: Curves on the plugin's screen
curves.summary: An equaliser on a Zynthian chain has a screen of its own that draws its response curve, and the curve follows every change you make.
curves.what: A plugin that declares a curve, such as the frequency response of omx eq8, gets a screen of its own, drawn by OpenMixer's panel renderer. The curve is not a picture: plugin-hostd computes it from the plugin's current settings each time it is drawn.
curves.where: On the chain's control screen, on the plugin's own pages.
curves.do: Turn a band's gain, frequency or width with the knobs: the curve is drawn again from the value you set.
curves.sees: The plugin's sections and their controls, with the curve drawn above them.
curves.notYet: The compressor's transfer curve (omx comp) is not drawn on Zynthian yet. It comes when omx-panel reads the compressor's own panel over the description plugin-hostd writes of it.

drawbars-xy.title: Drawbars and the XY screen answer the same touches
drawbars-xy.summary: The organ drawbars and the XY screen now answer the same touches, with the same timings, as every OpenMixer panel.
drawbars-xy.what: Zynthian's drawbar screen (setBfree's, and any organ with drawbars) and its XY screen now read your touches through OpenMixer's one gesture vocabulary. Zynthian's own drawing is kept: only what a touch means changed.
drawbars-xy.where: The drawbar screen of an organ, and the XY screen that sets two controls at once.
drawbars-xy.do: Drawbars: drag a drawbar up or down; slide sideways to set several in one stroke (each takes the height under your finger, and the ones you pass over in between follow); double-tap a drawbar to put it back to its default; the wheel or the arrow keys step the selected one. A long press is recognised, and does nothing on the drawbars yet. XY: drag the point; double-tap puts it back to its default; a long press leaves the screen; the arrow keys step it.
drawbars-xy.sees: The same drawbars and the same XY point as before, moving the way a finger expects.

meters.title: A plugin's own meters
meters.summary: A plugin's own meters, such as a compressor's gain reduction, are on their way to its screen: everything is in place on the panel side, and they are not drawn on Zynthian yet.
meters.what: A plugin can declare meters: omx comp declares its gain reduction and its input, output and key levels. Zynthian takes the meters a plugin's panel declares, or the ones plugin-hostd describes when the panel does not list them, and draws each from the readings plugin-hostd sends.
meters.notYet: On Zynthian today no plugin meter is drawn: the plugin-hostd release installed there does not pass a plugin's meters on to the screen yet. This page gets its picture when it does.

rta.title: A spectrum analyser on the plugin's screen
rta.summary: A real-time spectrum analyser on the plugin's screen, before and after the plugin and the difference: coming.
rta.what: omx-rta-read reads the spectrum a plugin receives and the one it gives back, and the difference between them, for the plugin's own screen. Measured on a Raspberry Pi 5, one reader costs between 0.6 and 3.4 percent of one core, without a single dropout.
rta.notYet: It reaches Zynthian with the next omx-dsp and omx-panel releases and a zynthian-ui change. This page then shows it.

panels.title: Plugin panels from the plugin's own declaration
panels.summary: A plugin's pages come from what the plugin declares: its path and text parameters, the meaning of each control, and no invented pages for a plugin such as Surge XT.

restart.title: A saved chain comes back whole after a restart
restart.summary: Restart Zynthian and a chain hosted by plugin-hostd comes back as you left it, with its MIDI routing and its mixer strip.
restart.what: A chain of plugin-hostd plugins is saved even when one of its plugins could not be built, it keeps its MIDI routing, and a chain that makes sound gets its strip in the mixer back.
restart.do: Nothing new: restart, or switch the Pi off and on.
restart.sees: The chain in the mixer with its strip, and its plugins in place.

names.title: Chains and plugins named by the plugin
names.summary: A chain shows its plugins by their own names, and JACK knows which plugin each hosted port belongs to.
names.what: A chain lists its plugin-hostd plugins by their names. Each hosted plugin's JACK client carries its plugin and its instance in JACK metadata, and a label that stays the same when the plugin's worker starts again.
names.where: In the chain's list of processors, and in any JACK tool that reads metadata, such as a patchbay.

updates.title: Updates come from signed release tags
updates.summary: Updating Zynthian installs OpenMixer's signed release tags, and the update check offers only what the update would take.
updates.what: update_zynthian.sh takes OpenMixer's signed release tags; the old path that followed the latest commit is gone. The update check in the menu offers an update only when there is a tag the updater would install. The image is built from the Open-Mixer forks.
updates.where: The update check and the update in Zynthian's admin menu.

language.title: Zynthian in the device's language
language.summary: What the OpenMixer libraries say on Zynthian is read in the device's language, Catalan included.
language.what: The messages and the plugin sentences of the OpenMixer libraries are read in the language the device is set to. Each language is one language pack, and a Catalan catalog is in. The libraries ship the tools their owners translate with.
language.where: The messages plugin-hostd gives and the plugin sentences in the menus.

presets.title: Presets that load back
presets.summary: Surge XT's CLAP presets on Zynthian, LV2 user presets saved as preset bundles, a preset you saved loads back, and a clear refusal when a preset does not apply.

plugin-paths.title: Plugins found where distributions install them
plugin-paths.summary: plugin-hostd looks where distributions put plugins and where Zynthian keeps them, says what it searches, reads CLAP plugins in bundles and takes the newest LV2 version.

qualification.title: Plugin qualification read from the system store
qualification.summary: The menus read each plugin's qualification from the system store the sync fills, and a disabled sync no longer fails.

workers.title: Each plugin runs locked down
workers.summary: Each plugin runs in a worker that cannot gain privileges or reach the daemon.
workers.what: A plugin-hostd worker runs with no_new_privs, without the daemon's open descriptors, and under a seccomp filter that denies the system calls a plugin has no business making. A plugin that crashes or misbehaves stays inside its worker.
workers.do: Nothing: every plugin hosted by plugin-hostd runs this way.

properties.title: Plugin properties, and refusals that say whether to try again
properties.summary: plugin-hostd's protocol reads and sets a plugin's properties, and a refusal says whether it is passing.
properties.what: The protocol relays property_list, property_info, property_get and property_set to a plugin instance, with text values quoted. A refusal now says whether it is transient, so a controller knows when trying again makes sense.
properties.where: In what Zynthian's interface, MOD-UI or any other controller can ask plugin-hostd.

measured.title: Measured on the Pi
measured.summary: The figures behind the Zynthian pages were measured on a Raspberry Pi 5.
measured.what: plugin-hostd's bench by rate and period, with each rate's safe minimum; a plugin's memory as RSS and PSS; real-time safety thread by thread; instruments and the thread pool on the Pi's cores; the analog loop through an RME interface at 48 and 96 kHz; and the memory controller on at boot, so a plugin's memory can be measured.
measured.where: The interim Zynthian benchmarks, and the notes on instruments on a Pi 5 and on how a plugin's memory is judged.

vangelis.title: The fork follows Zynthian vangelis
vangelis.summary: The Open-Mixer fork of zynthian-sys follows Zynthian's vangelis, with its rewritten update recipes and its websocket server.

libraries.title: One vocabulary: Zynthian reads the OpenMixer libraries
libraries.summary: zynthian-ui no longer writes its own copy of the protocol words, codes, scan documents, position law, gestures or compare slots: it reads them from plugin-hostd's Python client, omx-contract and omx-panel, which zynthian-sys installs.

releases.title: DEBs beside RPMs, one channel
releases.summary: Every OpenMixer library ships DEBs beside its RPMs from the one channel, and ordinary builds never take the staging repository.

testing.title: How the engine is tested
testing.summary: A written threat model, fuzzing that is proven to find what it is meant to find, and tests that are shown to fail when the code is broken.
testing.what: The engine has a threat model; its fuzzing is proven by sabotage, and its records and coverage are kept; patch names are checked; the self-tests are faster; and sabotage arms show that a test fails when the code it guards is broken.

name.title: FreeMixer is now Open-Mixer and OpenMixer
name.summary: The organisation is Open-Mixer and the product OpenMixer, in every package and on every page.
name.what: The GitHub organisation that was FreeMixer is Open-Mixer, and the product is OpenMixer. Every package, library and page was renamed.

how-we-work.title: How we work: checks on every change
how-we-work.summary: Quick checks on every pull request, the heavy runs on release tags, and commit messages checked before they land.
how-we-work.what: Every pull request runs the quick checks; the heavy runs happen on release tags and on demand. Builds use as many jobs as their share of the machine allows, package-manager calls have a time limit, commit messages are checked, build artifacts are kept for a set time, and an issue is closed by hand once its fix is proven.

hosting.title: Plugin hosting: one host for CLAP and LV2, three more omx effects, measured costs
hosting.summary: Every plugin insert now runs in one host, CLAP directly and LV2 through its adapter (mod-host is retired), and the omx ducker, doubler and tone join the effects you can add from the picker.

presets.title: Presets: a desk-wide preset library
presets.summary: Presets now live in a desk-wide library outside every session, saved in each plugin's own format, so LV2 presets you save are standard bundles other LV2 hosts can open.

curves-meters.title: Curves, meters and panels drawn from the shared libraries
curves-meters.summary: EQ, gate and compressor curves, meter ballistics, units and plugin panels now come from the shared omx-dsp, omx-panel and omx-contract libraries, so the console, Zynthian and any other host draw them identically.

languages.title: Languages and coded messages
languages.summary: Languages arrive as installable packs read at run time, and every refusal, warning and fault reaches the surface as a code worded in your language, never as English text.

web-surface.title: Web surface: menus and editing fixes
web-surface.summary: On a narrow screen the header's menus fold into one MENU cap that opens each menu as its own submenu, quickly, and FX tiles open on the first tap.

control24.title: Control|24: all 24 strips
control24.summary: A Digidesign Control|24 now drives all 24 of its strips from the console's strip order, a page of 24 at a time.

clock.title: Audio graph and clock robustness
clock.summary: A desktop sound-settings profile switch can no longer take the clock-master interface out of its pro-audio profile at boot, and the console asks for it back while running.

streams.title: Streams and the REST API
streams.summary: A stream subscriber can ask for lossless deltas (deltas=1) instead of whole bodies on large rows such as the edit history, and every row now declares its wire shape.

assistant.title: Assistant (MCP server)
assistant.summary: The MCP server answers project questions from its corpus, starts cold within 10 s, and its HTTP entry binds loopback with an optional bearer token.

packaging.title: Packaging, releases and the Open-Mixer name
packaging.summary: The project now publishes as OpenMixer from the Open-Mixer organisation, with packages built and install-tested on Fedora 44 and 45 and every library dependency held between a floor and a ceiling.

rta-design.title: RTA on Zynthian (design only)
rta-design.summary: The design for an analyser on Zynthian, drawn by the same renderer as the console, is settled; the analyser bands moving into omx-dsp are still in review.

how-changes-land.title: How a change reaches the console: settle, verify and deploy gates
how-changes-land.summary: Every change now reaches the console through checked lanes and signed settles: a scan for private references in every message, library pins at the served version, a verification reused only for the exact same tree, temporary files cleaned up, and a deploy that checks what it installs.
